messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category. Here are worked examples, then the case to code.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: I21

Example 3
Hospital course: A 34-year-old woman presented with fever, rigors, dysuria and right flank tenderness. Urine microscopy showed pyuria and culture grew Escherichia coli. Computed tomography showed a swollen right kidney with no abscess. She improved on intravenous ceftriaxone.
Answer: N10

Example 4
Hospital course: An 81-year-old woman was brought in after a fall at home. She could not weight-bear and the right leg was shortened and externally rotated. A pelvic radiograph showed a displaced subcapital fracture of the right femoral neck. She underwent hemiarthroplasty on day one.
Answer: S72

Example 5
Hospital course: A 19-year-old man presented with 18 hours of periumbilical pain that migrated to the right iliac fossa, with anorexia and a low-grade fever. There was guarding at McBurney's point and the white cell count was 15.2. Laparoscopy confirmed an inflamed, non-perforated appendix.
Answer: K35

Example 6
Hospital course: A 64-year-old woman with a history of oestrogen-receptor-positive breast carcinoma treated five years earlier presented with progressive thoracic back pain. Magnetic resonance imaging showed deposits in T7 and T9 with no cord compression. Biopsy confirmed deposits of breast origin and she received palliative radiotherapy to the spine.
Answer: C79

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [REDACTED]

Age: 70 years

Sex: Male

Medical History:

The patient was diagnosed with advanced renal cell carcinoma and was receiving Ipilimumab/Nivolumab therapy. He presented with new-onset fatigue and dizziness after two cycles of therapy.

Hospital Course:

During the hospital course, the patient underwent a physical examination, which revealed normal visual fields. Laboratory assessment showed mild hyponatremia, with low TSH and free T4. Morning ACTH and cortisol were also low. MRI brain showed pituitary enhancement.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Treatment:

Ipilimumab/Nivolumab therapy was temporarily stopped, and the patient was started on hydrocortisone 10mg/5mg in the morning and afternoon, respectively, as well as a weight-based dose of levothyroxine. The patient demonstrated clinical improvement and was restarted on PD-1 monotherapy.

Follow-up:

The patient was given "sick day" instructions for stress dosing of hydrocortisone and a medical alert bracelet. Key concepts of management involve high index of clinical suspicion, appropriate localization of endocrine dysfunction, hormone replacement, and close monitoring. Immune-related endocrine events are unique as the manifestations are often irreversible, and patients often require lifelong hormone replacement.

Hospital Disposition:

The patient was discharged from the hospital after clinical improvement. It is recommended that ICI is held for any-grade hypophysitis. Once patients demonstrate stability on hormonal replacement, ICI can be restarted. Higher-grade hypophysitis can be managed with an initial pulsed dose of corticosteroids. The patient was instructed to continue receiving follow-up medical care.

Answer with the three-character category only.

text:
This is immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced hypophysitis with secondary adrenal and thyroid insufficiency, so the picture is hypopituitarism. The ICD-10-AM options are:

- E23 (hypofunction and other disorders of the pituitary gland), which includes hypopituitarism and drug-induced hypopituitarism (E23.1).
- E89.3 (postprocedural hypopituitarism), which does not fit.
- E24.2 (drug-induced Cushing's syndrome), which does not fit either.

Hypophysitis itself has no specific code and is usually classed under E23.6 (other disorders of the pituitary gland). Either way, the category is E23.

**E23**
